findings.why_it_matters: The 20-21 row of the WHEN-COMPILED returned-value table is no longer a table row, so any tool or reader consuming the 15.99.3 table sees only positions 1 through 19 and the last two character positions of the 21-character returned value fall out of the structure. The transcription already has the correct convention for this exact situation — the identical CURRENT-DATE table split across pages 864/865 restarts with a '| **Character Positions** | **Contents** |' header row and continues the table — so page 968 is an inconsistent degradation, not a house style.
findings.suggested_repair: On the page-968 slice, restart the table the way page-865 does: emit '| **Character Positions** | **Contents** |' + separator, then '| 20-21 | Two numeric digits are returned ... the value 00 is returned. |'.

findings.why_it_matters: A stray pair of markdown bold markers has been wrapped around the terminating period of the returned-value expression; nothing in the printed page is emphasized there. The raw text now reads '+ 1)**.**' inside an arithmetic expression, and '**' is COBOL's exponentiation operator, so a reader or extraction tool taking the expression verbatim can misparse it. The sibling occurrence in 15.94.4 c) on page 958 is transcribed correctly as '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).'.
